stem: Find the number of points of intersection of the circle $x^2+y^2={=r*r}$ and the line $x-y+{=c}=0$
solution: Substitute into the circle: $x^2+(x+{=c})^2={=r*r}$, which simplifies to $2x^2+{=2*c}x+({=c*c-r*r})=0$.
The sign of $D$ gives the number of points: $D>0$ means 2, $D=0$ means 1, $D<0$ means 0. So there are {=2 if D > 0 else 0} points of intersection.
notes: Basic entry: substitute line into circle centred at origin, read the sign of D. Tangency excluded because 2r^2 = c^2 has no integer solution anyway. Answer 0 or 2.
